phases: The Words of the First Minute

listenings.text: I am Ingrid Vogel and I work at a university in Munich. Can I tell you the only thing I know about congresses? Nobody is comfortable. The people standing alone with a coffee are not unfriendly. They are waiting for somebody to speak first, exactly like you. In my first years I stood at the side of the room and I told myself that my English was not good enough. Then a colleague told me something I still use. She said: do not prepare a speech, prepare one question. You are not going there to perform. You are going there to ask. Now I approach two or three people every day at a congress, and I always start with the same sentence. What are you working on at the moment?

Dejair, it is Ayse. We are all in the coffee area on the first floor and I am looking at you from here, standing alone by the window with your phone. Come over. There are four of us and two of them work on nerve damage, so this is your table, not mine. Bring your phone, but put it in your pocket. One more thing, and then I stop. Do not say sorry for your English before you speak. I did that for years. People do not hear the mistake, they hear the apology, and then they think you are not sure about your science either. You are not here as a student of English. You are here as a researcher.
